feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: Breaking news, top national and world stories, politics, business and culture from NPR. Catch up on demand with NPR News Now, Up First and Consider This.

entry.title: European air traffic is targeted by new threats after a week of hoaxes
entry.summary: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats.

entry.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
entry.summary: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.

entry.title: Ex-lawmaker gets 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case
entry.summary: Au's arrest last year was the first publicly known prosecution under Macao's national security law since it was enacted in 2009.

entry.title: Hiring jumps: The economy added 165,000 jobs last month
entry.summary: The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.

entry.title: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch. And, Labor Department to release jobs report
entry.summary: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.

entry.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
entry.summary: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?

entry.title: 'He's got to go': Hakeem Jeffries calls for Hegseth's removal but stops short of impeachment
entry.summary: Speaking with Morning Edition, Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver.

entry.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
entry.summary: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."

entry.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
entry.summary: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

entry.title: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
entry.summary: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.
